• **Vaporisation** refers to the process of a liquid turning into a gas, either through evaporation or boiling.
 
• **Condensation** is the process where a gas turns into a liquid.
 
• Understanding these processes is crucial in fields such as chemistry, physics, and engineering.
 
• Each of these processes involves energy changes and plays a significant role in various natural and industrial applications.

questions.question: As per Article ________ of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:

__
 
• As per Article **75(3)** of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
• This implies that the entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is accountable to the Lok Sabha for its actions and policies.
 
• If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, they must collectively resign.
 
• This collective responsibility ensures that the executive branch of the government is answerable to the legislative branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of collective responsibility is fundamental to the parliamentary system of government.
 
• It ensures that the executive remains responsible and accountable to the legislature, and through it, to the people.
 
• This principle is essential for maintaining the stability and integrity of the government.
 
• Article 75 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibilities of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• Article 75(1) states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and the other ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• Article 75(2) mentions that the ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• Article 75(3) establishes the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.

• Although the Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law, they serve as moral obligations for every citizen.
 
• The idea behind these duties is to encourage responsible behavior and promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was appointed to make recommendations about Fundamental Duties, and many of its suggestions were incorporated into Article 51-A.

questions.question: Biological Diversity Act 2002 was passed by the Government of India. It fulfilled ideals of which article of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India?

• The **Biological Diversity Act 2002** was enacted by the Government of India to conserve biological diversity, ensure sustainable use of its components, and ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the use of biological resources.
 
• It fulfills the ideals of **Article 48A** of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India.
 
• **Article 48A** states that "The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country."

questions.question: A person borrowed Rs. 1760 at 6% per annum and Rs. 2240 at 9% per annum at simple interest for the same period. He had to pay Rs. 1536 in all as interest. Find the time (in years).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Calculate **interest for one year** for both parts.

Interest 1 = 1760 × 6% = ₹105.6

Interest 2 = 2240 × 9% = ₹201.6

Total interest per year = 105.6 + 201.6 = ₹307.2

Time = Total interest ÷ Yearly interest = 1536 ÷ 307.2 = 5 years

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**P₁** = ₹1760, **R₁** = 6% p.a.

**P₂** = ₹2240, **R₂** = 9% p.a.

**Total Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹1536

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd545641a56683b4b500716d2209f701dd4d37159e2297df1beab86ff1a9b953.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total SI = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ 1536 = [(1760 × 6 × T) ÷ 100] + [(2240 × 9 × T) ÷ 100]

⇒ 1536 = [10560T ÷ 100] + [20160T ÷ 100]

⇒ 1536 = 105.6T + 201.6T

⇒ 1536 = 307.2T

⇒ T = 1536 ÷ 307.2

⇒ T = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

Simple interest is calculated on the original principal amount only: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate per annum, and T is Time in years.

Total Amount

The total amount (A) payable after time T is the sum of the principal and the interest: A = P + SI = P × (1 + RT/100).

Effective Interest Rate

When multiple principals or rates are involved for the same time, the effective annual interest generated can be found by summing individual (P × R) values.

questions.question: A car covers 20 km in the first quarter of an hour, 25 km in the second quarter of that hour and 15 km in the third quarter. The average speed of the car (in km/h) over the entire journey is:

Average Speed = 60 ÷ (3/4) = 60 × (4/3) = 80 **km/h**

⇒ **Total Time** = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 **hr**

⇒ **Average Speed** = 60 ÷ (3/4)

⇒ **Average Speed** = 60 × (4/3)

⇒ **Average Speed** = 20 × 4 = 80 **km/h**

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a body travels with speeds v₁, v₂, v₃ for equal time intervals, Average Speed = (v₁ + v₂ + v₃) ÷ 3.

Average Speed for Equal Distance Intervals

If a body covers two equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, Average Speed = 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

questions.question: A man wishes to cover 1 km distance in river water. In still water he takes 12 minutes to cover it, but in the flowing river he takes 13 minutes. The speed of the flowing water of the river is:

Speed = Distance / Time

**Formula Used:**

Speed in still water = Distance / Time in still water

Speed in flowing water = Distance / Time in flowing water

Speed of river flow = Speed in flowing water - Speed in still water

**Calculation:**

Speed in still water = 1 km / 12 minutes = 1 km / (12/60 hours) = 1 km / 0.2 hours = 5 km/h

**∴ The speed of the flowing water of the river is (5/13) km/h.**

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work alone in 200 days, while B can complete the same piece of work alone in 100 days. In every three-day cycle, both A and B work on day 1, only A works on day 2, and only B works on day 3. This cycle continues till the work is completed. How many days in all does it take the duo to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete a piece of work alone in 200 days.

B can complete the same piece of work alone in 100 days.

In every three-day cycle:

- Both A and B work on day 1

- Only A works on day 2

- Only B works on day 3

**Concept:**

Calculate the work done in each 3-day cycle and then find the total number of cycles required to complete the work.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/200

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/100

**Calculation:**

Work done by A and B together on day 1:

⇒ (1/200) + (1/100) = 1/200 + 2/200 = 3/200

Work done by A on day 2:

⇒ 1/200

Work done by B on day 3:

⇒ 1/100

Total work done in each 3-day cycle:

⇒ 3/200 + 1/200 + 1/100 = 3/200 + 1/200 + 2/200 = 6/200 = 3/100

Total work to be done = 1 (whole work)

Number of 3-day cycles needed to complete the work:

⇒ Total work / Work done in each cycle = 1 / (3/100) = 100/3

Total days needed = Number of cycles × 3 days per cycle

⇒ (100/3) × 3 = 100 days

Since the work is completed in fractions of a cycle, we need to calculate the exact number of days:

100/3 = 33 cycles and 1/3 cycle remaining

For the remaining 1/3 cycle:

Day 1: Work done = 3/200 (A and B together)

Day 2: Work done = 1/200 (A alone)

Day 3: Work done = 1/100 (B alone)

Total work done in 1/3 cycle:

⇒ 1/3 × (3/200 + 1/200 + 1/100) = 1/3 × (3/100) = 1/100

Hence, the remaining work after 33 cycles:

⇒ 1 - (99/100) = 1/100

Additional day required to complete the remaining 1/100 of work by A alone:

⇒ 1/200 × 2 = 1/100

Total days:

⇒ 33 cycles × 3 days + 1 additional day = 99 + 2/3 days ≈ 99 (2/3) days

**∴ The correct answer is option 2: 99 (2/3) days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A alone completes work in = 200 days

B alone completes work in = 100 days

**Calculations:**

LCM of 200 and 100 = 200 (Total work = 200 units)

A’s 1 day work = 200 ÷ 200 = 1 unit

B’s 1 day work = 200 ÷ 100 = 2 units

Now, work in 3-day cycle:

Day 1: A + B = 1 + 2 = 3 units

Day 2: A = 1 unit

Day 3: B = 2 units

Total in 3 days = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6 units

We need 200 units, so:

⇒ 33 cycles (99 days) = 198 units

Remaining = 200 - 198 = 2 units

Next cycle: Day 1 (A + B) = 3 units > 2 units needed

So, Total days = 99 + 2/3 = 99 (2)/(3) days

**∴ The duo completes the work in 99 (2)/(3) days.**

questions.question: The cost price of 36 articles is the same as the selling price of N articles. If the profit is 20%, then the value of N is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** = (100 + **Profit%**) ÷ 100 = 120/100 = 6/5.

Given: **Cost price** of 36 articles = **Selling price** of N articles ⇒ 36 × CP = N × SP.

Rearranging the equation: SP/CP = 36/N.

Equating the two ratios: 36/N = 6/5 ⇒ 6N = 36 × 5 ⇒ N = 6 × 5 = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP of 36 articles = SP of N articles. **Profit** = 20%.

**Formula:** SP = CP × (100 + **Profit %**) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c31c6d0a9a2597c43cb798851b9d59bbd7455ee917335ada17f1da2b9192594.png] 

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 article be ₹1.

⇒ Total **Cost Price** of 36 articles = ₹36.

⇒ Given: **Selling Price (SP)** of N articles = **Cost Price** of 36 articles = ₹36.

⇒ **Cost Price** of N articles = ₹N.

⇒ **Profit %** = [(SP of N − CP of N) / CP of N] × 100

⇒ 20 = [(36 − N) / N] × 100

⇒ 20/100 = (36 − N) / N

⇒ 1/5 = (36 − N) / N

⇒ N = 5 × (36 − N)

⇒ N = 180 − 5N

⇒ 6N = 180

⇒ N = 180 ÷ 6 = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Relation for Article-Based Profit/Loss

If the CP of 'x' articles is equal to the SP of 'y' articles, then Profit or Loss % = [(x − y) / y] × 100. A positive result indicates **Profit**, and a negative result indicates **Loss**.

Selling Price and Cost Price Relationship

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 for profit cases, and SP = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100 for loss cases. This is fundamental for **percentage-based trade calculations**.

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**∴ The average speed for the complete journey is 99 km/h.**
